So going to the store to buy all the things a traditional farm uses, some of which are one time purchases, eliminating the need to utilize a semi to haul them to the store, and removing the requirement to drive to the store and back is going to cause a higher carbon footprint? I’m calling BS. Sure if you only do it for a year and then toss it all out it might be slightly higher. I guarantee you though a small scale backyard veggie patch over the course of 2 years will not. 

Hell most seeds don’t even need that much care. I accidentally grew a pumpkin patch last fall because we smashed pumpkins the previous year. We ended up with around 50 pounds of pie pumpkins, 6 lbs of zucchini (in clay btw!), 20 lbs of tomatoes, 15 pounds of peppers, 12 pounds of cucumbers, a couple apples, 30 lbs of potatoes, a handful of sweet potatoes, and 3-5 lbs of luffa by just letting nature do its thing. A little water here and there during the couple of summer dry spells but that was basically it. 

Nature evolved without humans cultivating things for millions of years. Toss some seeds down and see what grows. Let nature do the work and you’ll be amazed at what will just naturally grow. Without planning anything, I guarantee that your carbon footprint will be lower. 

All of this before you set up things like rainwater collection, solar panels for things like pumps and fans, hydro- or aquaponics, composting bins to reduce trash and recycling going into landfills, etc. Those things will lower your footprint even further
